title: Reduce observability allocations and introduce lightweight trace proxy
creator: Marina Soto
description:
Background:
Our runtime telemetry hotpath allocates heavily when instrumenting every request. Flame graphs and heap profiles show repeated small allocations from span context serialization, tags/label maps, and the OTLP exporter envelope. This drives CPU overhead and increases GC pressure on tail-latency sensitive endpoints (generation and KV cache paths).

Goal:
Reduce per-request allocations in the in-process telemetry path by introducing a lightweight trace proxy (trace-proxy) that batches, reuses buffers, and performs nop-filtering for common low-cardinality routes. The proxy is intended to be a minimal layer inside the runtime (single goroutine / event loop) that copies less, uses preallocated buffers and object pools, and emits compact envelopes to the existing async exporter.

Success criteria:
- Reduce allocations in the hotpath by >=50% (heap alloc/req) on synthetic traffic for chat/generation workloads.
- p99 generation latency should not regress more than 2% and p50 should improve for high-concurrency scenarios.
- No change to external telemetry format (OTLP) visible to downstream systems.
- Unit/integration tests and a migration flag to opt-out (rollout safety).

Technical approach:
1) Spike and prototype (done): implement an in-process trace-proxy that accepts framed span events, uses a sync.Pool of buffers, and deduplicates common tag sets. The prototype shows ~53% allocation reduction on the local benchmark for 8k token requests.
2) Replace map[string]string label encoding with a compact stable-index tag table for the runtime. Tags are interned per-worker and referenced by small integers in the proxy envelope.
3) Defer heavy OTLP envelope construction to the exporter worker: the proxy emits compact framed messages and the existing exporter reconstructs OTLP on flush.
4) Add a runtime flag (telemetry.proxy_enabled) and canary the change under runtime-2.3 for 10% of production traffic via rollout rules.
5) Add feature gates and metrics: proxy_inserts, proxy_drops, pool_hit_rate, proxy_alloc_reduction_delta.

Rollout and safety:
- Start with internal staging, run CRC and canary on dedicated capacity only. 
- Provide an emergency revert via feature flag and a kill-switch at the node level.
- Preflight: integration tests to ensure no lost spans for high-cardinality traces and validate downstream dashboards after conversion.

Notes on scope and exclusions:
- This ticket focuses on runtime/in-process optimizations. Upgrading OTLP exporters or changing external observability backends will be separate tickets.
- Does not modify downstream analytic pipelines or sampling policies (only internal representation and batching).
acceptance_criteria: Hotpath heap allocations reduced by >=50% on standard benchmark (compare before/after profiles)
p99 latency regression <=2% in production canary; p50 improved under high concurrency
Proxy feature gated behind telemetry.proxy_enabled and can be rolled back immediately
End-to-end tests that validate no loss of span attributes and correct OTLP reconstruction
